summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: discrete mathematics (sets, functions, induction, summations, recurrences, basic number theory and elementary group/ring/field vocabulary), an algorithms course (recursion, divide and conquer, schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication, the FFT at the level of the divide-and-conquer recursion, solving recurrences), single-variable calculus (limits, exponentials, logarithms) and one course in linear algebra and complex numbers. They know Turing machines and big-O at an introductory level, but have not studied fast integer multiplication beyond Karatsuba, Schönhage-Strassen or Harvey-van der Hoeven, numerical error analysis, bilinear forms over finite fields, matrix factorizations such as Bruhat decompositions, or tape-level algorithm engineering.

known.name: Binary representation and schoolbook arithmetic
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a string of bits (or digits in base b) with the leftmost digit most significant, and addition and multiplication by hand take time quadratic in the length using carries.

known.name: Floor, ceiling and logarithms
known.gloss: The notations floor(x), ceiling(x), lg x = log_2 x and the iterated logarithm, together with the rule that an integer v needs floor(log_2 v)+1 bits.

known.name: Exponentials and elementary inequalities
known.gloss: Calculus-level facts on exponentials and powers with real exponents, limits, and simple inequalities such as 1+x <= e^x used to compare growth rates.

known.name: Summation, telescoping sums and geometric series
known.gloss: Finite sums written with Σ, sums in which consecutive terms cancel, and the closed form of geometric series.

known.name: Recurrences and the recursion tree
known.gloss: A cost T(n) defined in terms of smaller instances, solved by unrolling or a recursion tree to obtain a closed-form bound.

known.name: Karatsuba and classical multiplication algorithms
known.gloss: The schoolbook O(n^2) multiplication and Karatsuba's divide-and-conquer O(n^{log_2 3}) multiplication, as taught in algorithms courses, as the baseline against which faster methods are compared.

known.name: Recursion, call stack and subroutines
known.gloss: A procedure calling smaller instances of itself, with a stack of suspended calls, and the idea of using a procedure as a black box with a stated cost.

known.name: Sets, functions, bijections and permutations
known.gloss: Index sets such as [n]={0,...,n-1}, product sets, functions and their composition, and permutations as bijections of a finite set.

known.name: Mathematical induction and proof techniques
aliases: induction on the number of steps
known.gloss: Standard proof methods for correctness and cost claims: induction, contradiction, and invariants maintained across steps.

known.name: Prime numbers and trial division
known.gloss: A prime has no divisors besides 1 and itself; integers are uniquely products of primes; primality of small numbers can be found by dividing by all smaller candidates.

known.name: Groups, rings and fields
known.gloss: Basic abstract-algebra vocabulary: sets with addition and multiplication satisfying axioms, with fields (such as the rationals, the complex numbers and the two-element field F_2) allowing division, and cyclic groups Z/qZ.

known.name: XOR and arithmetic over F_2
known.gloss: The exclusive-or of two bits is their sum modulo 2, applied coordinatewise to bit strings, and is its own inverse.

known.name: Special matrices and matrix algebra
known.gloss: Matrix multiplication, inverses and transposes, and the identity, diagonal, permutation and triangular matrices, together with standard basis vectors e_j.

known.name: Triangle inequality and norm bounds
known.gloss: The modulus of a sum is at most the sum of moduli, used to bound approximation errors that add.

known.name: Rational numbers and dyadic fractions
known.gloss: Quotients of integers, and in particular numbers whose denominator is a power of two, which have finite binary expansions.

known.name: Deterministic algorithms and worst-case time
known.gloss: An algorithm with no randomness whose cost is the maximum number of steps over all inputs of a given length, with a single pass over input called linear time.

known.name: Entrywise operations on arrays and vectors
known.gloss: Operations applied independently to each coordinate of a list or multi-indexed array, and the identification of polynomials, vectors and arrays with coefficient lists.
